experiment_template.research_question: Does unified bounded stateless tokenizer recovery eliminate single zero-response transport censoring without model-token cost?
stop_conditions: No favorable rerun or task replacement.
No task, state, order, prompt, context/model cap, total-token cap, threshold or scorer change.
Only stateless tokenizer transport retry parity may change.

records.falsifier: Either tokenizer path differs in retry eligibility, request bytes change, more than two physical attempts occur, a model request is created, an excluded failure retries, failed attempts disappear, logical call budgets change, or a single eligible first-attempt failure still stops the live sequence.
records.mechanism: Use one shared retry classification and attempt envelope for request-prompt and index/state tokenizers. After request-failed with zero response bytes, record the first attempt and retry the exact serialized bytes once. Cache only a valid success. All other failures remain terminal.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash exposed 8K ContextBench development tasks; useful reasoning-state continuity after actual recycling, with the fixed acceptance target and cumulative model input plus output tokens.
records.statement: Applying one identical-body retry to every stateless tokenizer measurement path will prevent a single zero-response tokenizer failure from censoring GLM-5.3-flash 8K ContextBench trajectories without adding cumulative model input plus output tokens.

experiment_template.research_question: Should a fully accounted local branch failure censor only that branch?
stop_conditions: Shared ancestry, freeze, accounting or provider-integrity failures still stop globally.

records.falsifier: Continuation contaminates another branch, hides missingness, changes denominators, reruns a failed identity, or provides no additional decision-relevant evidence.
records.mechanism: Classify ancestry, accounting and shared-prefix failures as shared stops, but record a fully accounted terminal branch failure as missing and continue later independent cells. Never rerun or replace the failed branch.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash exposed 8K ContextBench development tasks; useful reasoning-state continuity after actual recycling, with the fixed acceptance target and cumulative model input plus output tokens.
records.statement: Censoring only a locally failed GLM-5.3-flash 8K branch while continuing independent frozen cells will retain more ContextBench information per cumulative model input plus output tokens than stopping the whole sequence.

experiment_template.research_question: Does a shared-prefix post-recycle fork distinguish causal ARE state benefit from pre-exposure model variance?
stop_conditions: Any snapshot or pre-treatment identity mismatch stops the pair.
No threshold or state-content change within the causal study.
Retain every repetition and never select a lucky seed.

records.falsifier: Branches differ before treatment, snapshot clone changes any bound state, control sees state, treatment lacks its declared presentation, repeated branch estimates remain too unstable for the fixed threshold, or the design cannot account every model input/output token.
records.mechanism: Run one common prefix until an actual recycle boundary, freeze its task, repository, delivery, ledger and prompt state, then clone it into control and treatment branches. Apply state only to treatment on the first post-boundary dispatch. Repeat branch pairs from exact prefix snapshots and randomize branch order; score treatment effects only after exposure.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash exposed 8K ContextBench development tasks; useful reasoning-state continuity after actual recycling, with the fixed acceptance target and cumulative model input plus output tokens.
records.statement: Forking control and state from the same exact pre-recycle GLM-5.3-flash 8K trajectory and repeating post-boundary branches makes ContextBench state effects causally identifiable within cumulative model input plus output tokens.

experiment_template.research_question: Does evidence-only state have no criterion-complete causal benefit?

records.falsifier: A valid repeated shared-prefix study meets the fixed quality, completion, integrity and model-token criteria.
records.mechanism: Once the instrument is valid, semantic interpretation or task-specific variance may still dominate deterministic continuity.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash exposed 8K ContextBench development tasks; useful reasoning-state continuity after actual recycling, with the fixed acceptance target and cumulative model input plus output tokens.
records.statement: Deterministic state has no reliable causal benefit for GLM-5.3-flash ContextBench at 8K after valid shared-prefix control.

selection.reason: Round 17 directly exposed retry-policy asymmetry: an eligible zero-response request-tokenizer failure stopped the matrix while the parallel index/state tokenizer already had bounded recovery. Unify the capability before changing missing-data execution policy or interpreting H25.
